chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from 'Amr ibn Shimir from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to, when intending a matter of Hajj or Umrah or trade or purchase or manumission, purify himself, then pray two rak'ahs of Istikhara, reciting in them Surah al-Hashr and Surah ar-Rahman, then reciting the two Mu'awwidhat and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad'.

Then he would say: 'O Allah, if such and such is good for me in my religion and my world and my Hereafter and in the immediate and delayed aspects of my affair, then facilitate it for me in the best of ways. O Allah, if such and such is bad for me in my religion and my world and my Hereafter and in the immediate and delayed aspects of my affair, then turn it away from me in the best of ways. My Lord, make me firm upon my guidance even if I dislike that or my soul rejects it.'

key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The two Mu'awwidhat (Surah al-Falaq and Surah an-Nas)
key_terms.عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ: The immediate and delayed aspects of my affair

ai.seo_question: What is the specific method and dua for Istikhara prayer according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Imami tradition of performing Istikhara with specific Quranic recitations, notably Surah Al-Hashr and Surah Ar-Rahman, reflecting a deep reliance on divine wisdom over personal desire. The supplication’s emphasis on 'best of ways' and acceptance even if one dislikes the outcome underscores the Shia concept of *rida* (contentment) with Allah’s decree, linking ritual prayer to spiritual surrender.
